Specs are typically "optimal performance" meaning the 1 hour - or 2 hours if you are lucky - of the day the sun hits the panels at the correct angle to produce full power, and power drops off significantly outside of the 3 hours around noon. If there is cloud cover, or even a shady spot on any part of a panel, the output will typically drop below 50% output.

So a 100watt panel will provide close to 100 watts when all of the conditions are perfect, but then only provide an average of around 50 watts for the 6 to 8 hours of usable sunlight.

That's why houses that only typically average 2 kilowatts of power usage during a day would be recommended to install 4kw or more of solar. Batteries are must if not connected to the grid.
